heroHeadline: NOC Reopens Sharara Pipeline Valve After $95M Closure, as UNSMIL Warns Oil Disruptions Could Trigger UN Sanctions
heroSubtitle: Libya's National Oil Corporation said Saturday, Sep 26 evening it had reopened Valve No. 7 on the Sharara–Zawiya pipeline and resumed regular crude pumping, ending a five-day closure — which had cut output at Libya's largest field from ~300-350K bpd to ~100-105K bpd — that NOC said cost roughly $95 million; no force majeure was ever formally declared. Hours earlier, UNSMIL had warned that continued disruption of the pipeline 'is adversely affecting Libya's principal source of national income' and cautioned that actions undermining oil infrastructure 'may constitute grounds for the imposition of measures' under Security Council Resolution 2213. No new assassinations or oil-infrastructure drone strikes were confirmed this period; the political dispute over a reported Haftar power-sharing deal, which Grand Mufti Al-Gharyani warned against on Sep 24, remains unresolved.
